Why Scarborough Corporations Choose Gondaliya CPA for Corporate Tax Filing

Scarborough is one of the most commercially dense and culturally diverse districts in the Greater Toronto Area — home to over 632,000 residents and more than 18,000 registered businesses spanning food manufacturing, import/export trade, restaurants, construction, healthcare professional corporations and a rapidly expanding real estate development corridor along the Eglinton East LRT and Scarborough Centre. As the eastern anchor of the City of Toronto, Scarborough's economy is built on its unmatched cultural diversity — the largest South Asian, Caribbean, Chinese, Filipino and East African business communities in Ontario operate side by side along the Lawrence Avenue, Markham Road, Kennedy Road and Kingston Road commercial corridors.

Scarborough's food manufacturing sector is one of the largest in the GTA. Hundreds of food production companies — halal meat processing, South Asian packaged foods, Caribbean frozen goods, Chinese bakeries, Filipino specialty products and East African spice manufacturing — operate across the industrial corridors south of Highway 401 and along Birchmount Road. These businesses face the most complex HST classification demands in Ontario: zero-rated basic groceries vs. taxable prepared foods at 13%, with the distinction hinging on packaging, portion size, heating and point-of-sale presentation. CRA audits Scarborough food manufacturers at the product level — a single SKU misclassification on a high-volume product line produces a five-figure HST reassessment.

Scarborough's import/export trade corridor — driven by diaspora business networks connecting Toronto to South Asia, the Caribbean, China, the Philippines and East Africa — generates significant volumes of CBSA-collected import HST, customs duty obligations under international trade agreements and foreign affiliate reporting requirements (T1134/T1135). Many Scarborough trade businesses maintain supplier deposits, real estate holdings or bank accounts in their countries of origin without filing the required foreign property disclosure forms — exposing them to $2,500 per year in CRA non-filing penalties.

Gondaliya CPA has a Scarborough office at 24 Clementine Square, directly serving corporations across Scarborough Town Centre, the Golden Mile, Agincourt, Malvern, West Hill, Highland Creek and the Eglinton East corridor. Our licensed CPA team understands the specific deduction profiles of Scarborough's dominant industries — food manufacturing, import/export trade, restaurants, construction and healthcare — and files every T2 with the documentation that prevents Toronto East TSO reviews from escalating. Flat-fee from $400, no hourly billing.

Food Manufacturing — Birchmount Corridor

Scarborough Halal Meat Processor — HST Correction and CCA Reclassification

A Scarborough halal meat processing corporation had been charging 13% HST on all products including zero-rated unprocessed and minimally processed meats. Over three years, $196,000 in HST had been over-collected on zero-rated products. Simultaneously, $320,000 in meat processing equipment (commercial grinders, vacuum sealers, blast freezers, packaging lines) had been classified under CCA Class 8 (20%) instead of Class 53 (50% M&P). We corrected the HST classification at the product level, filed amended returns and reclassified the equipment.

✓ $196,000 HST correction + $19,400 CCA refund on amended returns
Import/Export — Markham Road Corridor

Scarborough South Asian Textile Importer — Import HST ITC and T1135 Filing

A Scarborough textile and garment importer sourcing from India and Bangladesh had not been claiming ITCs on $168,000 in CBSA-collected import HST over two years — the bookkeeper had recorded all border charges as a single customs expense. The corporation also held $340,000 in supplier deposits in Indian bank accounts without filing T1135, exposing it to $5,000 in CRA non-filing penalties. We separated the import HST from customs duties, filed amended GST/HST returns and prepared the T1135 forms.

✓ $168,000 HST ITCs recovered + $5,000 T1135 penalty exposure eliminated
Restaurant — Lawrence Avenue

Scarborough Caribbean Restaurant Group — Cash Revenue Reconciliation and Holdco

A Caribbean restaurant group operating three locations along Lawrence Avenue East had inconsistent POS-to-bank deposit reconciliation, with CRA flagging $92,000 in unexplained deposits across two years as potential unreported revenue. Our review traced every deposit to its source — $64,000 was shareholder loan contributions (personal funds deposited to cover payroll), $18,000 was catering deposits received in advance and $10,000 was a one-time insurance settlement. We documented each deposit with supporting evidence and resolved the CRA review. We also established a holdco to separate investment income across the three restaurant corporations.

✓ $92,000 unreported income allegation reversed — holdco implemented for 3-entity group

Common CRA Compliance Issues for Scarborough Corporations

CRA's Toronto East TSO processes Scarborough T2 returns with documented focus areas reflecting the district's food manufacturing, import/export and restaurant concentration.

Food HST Classification — Zero-Rated vs. Taxable

Scarborough's food manufacturers produce products spanning the full HST spectrum. Unprocessed and minimally processed meats, basic grains, raw produce and canned goods are zero-rated at 0%. Prepared foods (heated, single-serving, ready-to-eat, sold with utensils) are taxable at 13%. CRA audits Scarborough food manufacturers at the SKU level — the distinction between a zero-rated basic grocery and a taxable prepared food often depends on packaging, portion size or how the product is displayed at point of sale.

Cash Revenue — Restaurant Bank Deposit Analysis

CRA's most aggressive audit technique for Scarborough restaurants is the bank deposit analysis. CRA totals every deposit in every business bank account and compares the total to reported revenue. Every unexplained deposit — shareholder contributions, personal funds, advance catering deposits, insurance proceeds — is treated as unreported income unless you can document the source. Monthly bank reconciliation that identifies every deposit is the only reliable defence.

Import HST ITC vs. Customs Duty Separation

Scarborough's import/export corridor generates significant CBSA-collected import HST that is fully recoverable as ITCs. Customs duties are not recoverable — they are added to inventory cost. Recording all CBSA border charges in a single expense line without separating import HST from customs duties is the most common bookkeeping error for Scarborough importers and costs thousands per year in unclaimed ITCs.

T1135 Foreign Property Disclosure

Scarborough's diaspora business communities frequently maintain bank accounts, real estate holdings, supplier deposits and investment accounts in India, China, the Caribbean, the Philippines and East Africa. Corporations (and their shareholders) with specified foreign property exceeding $100,000 at any time during the year must file T1135. Non-filing penalties start at $2,500 per year and can reach $25,000 for repeated non-compliance. CRA's Toronto East TSO has increased T1135 enforcement across Scarborough.

How does HST apply to food manufactured in Scarborough?
Unprocessed and minimally processed foods (raw meats, grains, canned goods) are zero-rated at 0% HST. Prepared foods (heated, portioned, ready-to-eat) are taxable at 13%. CRA audits food HST at the SKU level — the classification depends on packaging, portion size and point-of-sale presentation. Scarborough food manufacturers must classify every product correctly. HST Guide →
What is T1135 and does my Scarborough business need to file it?
T1135 is the Foreign Income Verification Statement required when a Canadian corporation (or its shareholders) holds specified foreign property exceeding $100,000 at any time during the year. This includes foreign bank accounts, real estate, supplier deposits and shares of non-resident corporations. Non-filing penalties start at $2,500 per year. CRA's Toronto East TSO has increased T1135 enforcement across Scarborough.
How do Scarborough importers recover HST paid at the border?
HST collected by CBSA on imported goods is fully recoverable as an ITC on your GST/HST return. Customs duties are not recoverable — they are added to inventory cost. Keep import HST and customs duties in separate bookkeeping accounts. Recording CBSA charges as a single expense line costs Scarborough importers thousands per year in unclaimed ITCs. GST/HST Guide →
What is the Small Business Deduction and does my Scarborough corporation qualify?
The SBD reduces the federal rate from 15% to 9% on the first $500,000 of active business income for CCPCs. Combined with Ontario's 3.2%, qualifying Scarborough CCPCs pay 12.2% — saving up to $30,000 per year vs. the 26.5% general rate. We confirm CCPC status on every T2 we prepare.
